result.summary:
REVIEWER verdict: PASS. The ISS-0001 fix is a real fix, not a crutch. The three reads now go through the existing readTextFile (tools/src/util.js), the helper that exists for exactly this, and report codes the design already defines. There is no catch-all that would hide other errors. No blocking findings; nothing in the change erodes the bar. No Q7-Q11 surface is touched.

HOW I CHECKED (my own runs). Scratch: my folder scratchpad/rev-iss0001. Each case got a fresh copy of all of sai/ without node_modules. I ran the fixed tools/src/cli.js with --root <copy>. Before and after each run I took a strict listing of every entry (folders too) with mode, mtime in ns and sha256.

1 SCOPE / DIFF. sai/ has no git history, so the baseline is RELEASE-VALIDATOR's clean copy from 2026-09-28 (scratchpad/rv3.rLqu/sai, mtimes preserved). The developer's scratchpad/orig is byte-identical to it. diff -rq of that copy against tools/ (excluding node_modules): only src/validate.js, src/apply.js, src/cli.js and test/cli.test.js differ. util.js, snapshot.js, package.json, package-lock.json, eslint.config.js and .prettierignore are byte-identical. The code diff:
- validate.js checkVerdict: 4 lines replaced by readTextFile; message 'must exist' -> 'must be a readable file'.
- apply.js STATE.md read: readTextFile; message 'STATE.md not found' -> 'STATE.md missing, not a file or unreadable'; import added.
- cli.js snapshot-diff read: readTextFile; message 'snapshot not found' -> 'snapshot missing, not a file or unreadable'; import added.
- cli.test.js: tree import, a failsCleanly helper and 4 tests; no existing test changed.
mtime scan since 16:23:19Z: in tools/ only these 4 files changed. Everything else that changed belongs to the parallel agents (docs/requirements.yaml, handoffs/BP-20260930-01, handoffs/PO-20260930-01). Nothing in the repo depends on the old message texts. Scope equals the issue's three places plus tests; no scope creep.

2 THE THREE CASES (fixed CLI; copies of the real run WF06-20260926-01, which validates OK on the copy).
- verdict-2.md as a folder, verdict-1.md as a folder, verdict-2.md chmod 000, verdict-2.md missing: validate exit 1, "E_VERDICT_MD verdict-N.md: must be a readable file, mention the chosen idea and contain '## Ограничения'", 0 stack-trace lines, tree unchanged.
- The same breakage through apply-verdict, with proposed-actions.json and apply-report.json removed first so any write would show: exit 1, E_VERDICT_MD, 0 trace lines, unchanged. Control on the same copy without the breakage: exit 0 'applied recommend' and both files created, which proves the listing catches writes.
- STATE.md as an empty folder, as a folder with a file inside, chmod 000, and missing (run outputs removed first), also on WF06-20260925-01: apply-verdict exit 1, "E_STATE_ANCHOR STATE.md: STATE.md missing, not a file or unreadable", 0 trace lines, unchanged.
- snapshot-diff with a folder as <after>, a folder as <before>, <after> chmod 000, and <after> missing: exit 2, "E_USAGE: snapshot missing, not a file or unreadable: <path>", 0 trace lines, unchanged. Controls: equal snapshots exit 0; differing snapshots exit 1 with 3 'changed' lines.
- The pre-fix CLI on the same three setups: exit 1 each, 'Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read' and 8-10 '    at' lines; snapshot-diff exits 1 instead of 2. So the issue reproduces, and the fix removes it.
- Equivalence on valid input. Old vs new CLI on both real runs (validate OK; apply-verdict 'applied recommend' after a stale line in the block) give identical resulting file contents. snapshot-diff on regular files, 4 input/--allow combinations: identical stdout, stderr and exit codes.

3 TESTS. Each new test runs the real CLI and asserts, through failsCleanly: the exit code, the §6 error line (anchored regex), no /^\s+at /m on stderr (the pattern of the existing design §9 Q10 test), and tree(dir) unchanged (Q5).
Red check (mine): the new cli.test.js on the pre-fix sources in a full sai/ copy gives 115 tests, 111 pass, and exactly the 4 new tests fail, for the right reason (stderr is an EISDIR stack trace; snapshot-diff exits 1, expected 2).
Each test uses its own mkdtemp, and chmod is restored in finally. The unreadable test needs a non-root user: same comment and idiom as the existing E_SOURCE_CHANGED test (tools/test/validate.run.test.js:113-123). Run as root it fails loudly rather than being skipped, so no Q6 issue. I ran as uid 501.

4 Q6. grep over tools/src, tools/test, eslint.config.js and package.json for .skip/.todo/.only, {skip:}, eslint-disable, prettier-ignore, '|| true', process.exit(0) and exitCode = 0: no matches. The config files are unchanged (point 1).

5 IDIOM (decisions/0002: Node 22, prettier, eslint, node:test). readTextFile is the established helper (validate.js checkRun, prepare.js), and the new messages reuse its existing wording 'missing, not a file or unreadable'. Imports keep the existing order, and the tests follow the cli.test.js style and precedents. Consistent.

6 CHECK. cd tools && npm run check (node v22.21.1, npm 10.9.4) -> exit 0. Output: 'All matched files use Prettier code style!'; 'eslint . --max-warnings 0' with no findings; '1..115', '# tests 115', '# pass 115', '# fail 0', '# cancelled 0', '# skipped 0', '# todo 0'. The new tests are 'ok 22' to 'ok 25'.

OBSERVATIONS (non-blocking; no rework of this change)
O1 INFO. snapshot-diff now rejects non-regular inputs. Bash process substitution, snapshot-diff <(cat a) <(cat b), gives E_USAGE exit 2; before the fix it gave exit 0. There is no documented or recorded use: sai/ has no '<(', /dev/stdin or /dev/fd, and every recorded invocation passes files. This follows from readTextFile's contract and the issue. Fix: DOC-UPDATER says 'regular files' for <before>/<after> in design §7.
O2 LOW, for the follow-up tests. tree() (tools/test/helpers.js:350) lists regular files only, so it cannot see a folder added or removed, or a mode change. Not relevant to this change: my strict listing found no change of any kind. The sweep in I2 covers mkdirSync paths (prepare.js:135). Fix: its failure tests should compare a listing that includes folders.
O3 For ORCH. REQ-ANALYST's open question (handoffs/BP-20260930-01/step-00a-req-analyst-r3.json) asks whether the ISS-0001 change to cli.js affects REQ-006's step-4 snapshot-diff. snapshot.js is byte-identical. For regular files, snapshot-diff output and exit codes are identical before and after the fix (point 2).

DEVELOPER'S result.issues: RULINGS
Each was reproduced with the fixed CLI on a fresh copy of sai/. Where STATE.md had to need a rewrite, I inserted one stale line inside the existing wf06 block; markers and the owner's section stay intact. Control: apply exit 0 and STATE.md rewritten.

I1 Partial write in apply-verdict: CONFIRMED, MEDIUM.
- proposed-actions.json as a folder: STATE.md is rewritten (15345 -> 15334 bytes), then 'Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read', 8 trace lines, exit 1.
- apply-report.json as a folder (outputs removed first): STATE.md is rewritten AND proposed-actions.json created, then EISDIR, exit 1.
- Broader than reported. Run folder chmod 555 (outputs absent): STATE.md rewritten, then 'EACCES: permission denied, open', exit 1. apply-report.json chmod 444: STATE.md rewritten, then EACCES, exit 1.
Location: tools/src/apply.js:100-107. It writes STATE.md first, with no pre-check and no atomicity, so the class is any write failure after the first write. The proposed pre-check 'absent or a regular file' would close only the folder variants, not permission or disk-full failures.
Why MEDIUM, not LOW: it breaks design §5 (any issue means nothing is written) and the very condition ISS-0001 was rated LOW on ('падает до записи'). Between the crash and a re-run, STATE.md points at a proposed-actions.json that does not exist.
Why not HIGH: it needs a deliberate folder or permission change. A re-run after removing the obstacle converges: I verified 'applied recommend', then 'unchanged', with bytes identical to the real run outputs.
Fix (CODE-DESIGNER, then BACKEND-DEV): design the write phase so a failed write cannot leave a half-applied state, e.g. write each target to a temp file beside it and then rename, with STATE.md last as the commit point. Add a §6 code for a failed write. One test per target and per failure kind (folder, read-only file, read-only folder), asserting exit code, error line, no trace and an unchanged listing that includes folders.

I2 Six more stack-trace paths: ALL SIX CONFIRMED. Each gives exit 1 with a Node trace (7-10 '    at' lines) and writes nothing (strict listing unchanged).
a) apply-verdict, STATE.md chmod 444 and needing a change: EACCES open at the first write (apply.js:105). LOW. If STATE.md needs no change, apply proceeds normally.
b) snapshot, <out-file> is a folder: EISDIR open (cli.js:145). LOW.
c) snapshot, a file under --root unreadable (ideas/README.md chmod 000): EACCES open (snapshot.js:11). LOW.
d) snapshot, --root does not exist: ENOENT scandir (util.js:71 listFiles). LOW, but a plausible typo (Q10 'кривой ввод'); the follow-up should start with it.
e) prepare-run, runs is a file: ENOTDIR mkdir (prepare.js:135). Control prepare-run on a normal copy: exit 0 'prepared'. LOW.
f) validate, run folder mode 300: EACCES scandir (validate.js:144 checkUnknownLensFiles). LOW.
Two more of the same class that the developer did not list (found by me):
g1) snapshot, the parent folder of <out-file> is missing (e.g. a mistyped '<вне проекта>/' folder in WF-06 steps 0 and 6): ENOENT open (cli.js:145).
g2) snapshot, --root is a file: ENOTDIR scandir (util.js:71).
Both exit 1 with a trace and write nothing. LOW; g1 is as plausible as d.
Note: c, d, f and g2 are read errors. Design §6 already promises that read errors never print a trace ('Ошибки чтения и разбора никогда не выводят трассировку стека'), so these contradict the design as written. a, b, e and g1 are write errors, which have no §6 code, so they need a design decision (I agree with the developer).
Fix: one follow-up issue that sweeps every uncaught fs call in tools/src, each with a test and with codes decided by CODE-DESIGNER: apply.js:103/105, cli.js:145, prepare.js:135/136/138, snapshot.js:11, util.js:71, validate.js:144/606.

I3 PROCESS (Q13 candidate): CONFIRMED. ISS-0001 listed 3 paths; the developer found 6 more, and I found 2 more plus 2 more partial-write variants. [образец] already records this class: [образец]/docs/anti-patterns.md:2227 (a mechanism applied to two of three sibling code paths), :2439 (a fix that missed a sibling write path) and :2475 (a fix that still missed a third sibling). Fix: DOC-UPDATER adds a Sai AP entry that cites them: when fixing a class of defect, grep every call site and fix or list each one in the same work.

I4 DOC: CONFIRMED. Design §6 'Когда' does not name the cases these codes now cover:
- E_VERDICT_MD: verdict-N.md missing, not a file or unreadable;
- E_STATE_ANCHOR: STATE.md missing, not a file or unreadable;
- E_USAGE: a snapshot-diff input that is missing, not a file or unreadable.
This is not a silent divergence. The missing-file mappings pre-date the fix (tools/test/apply.state.test.js:19 'E_STATE_ANCHOR: STATE.md missing'; the old cli.js 'snapshot not found'), the issue prescribes these codes, and the developer raised the gap. Fix: DOC-UPDATER updates §6, plus §7 per O1, in this ISS-0001 route (Q14).

THE REAL REPO WAS NOT TOUCHED BY THIS REVIEW. STATE.md sha256 8c7cb84c... is unchanged. runs/ is unchanged: WF06-20260926-01 apply-report.json b80e6faf..., proposed-actions.json 8075c20f..., folder mtime 2026-09-28. The only files in sai/ changed since my start are the parallel agents' (docs/requirements.yaml, handoffs/BP-20260930-01/*, handoffs/PO-20260930-01/*).
One slip of mine, corrected: a setup snippet moved a scratch copy's STATE.md to /tmp/.x. I checked it was the copy (different inode; same bytes as the unchanged real file) and deleted it.

NEXT. TEST-RUNNER, per the ISS-0001 route. Then DOC-UPDATER with I3, I4 and O1. ORCH registers I1 (MEDIUM) and I2 (LOW, one sweep issue with the call-site list above).
